s1.syndrome_frame: subacute onset of tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core in a patient with immunocompromised state
salient_findings: tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions
sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells
key_facts: 74-year-old woman with chronic lymphocytic leukemia
complex karyotype with TP53 mutation and trisomy 12
receiving zanubrutinib and subcutaneous immunoglobulin replacement
hospitalized for pulmonary sepsis in May 2022
developed grade 4 neutropenia for over 15 days
febrile peak
skin lesions appeared on lower limbs and then upper limbs
zanubrutinib was discontinued on 25 June
oral itraconazole was begun on 25 June
histopathological examination showed severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation
angioinvasive microbial structures were seen
sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells were seen

shortlist.label: Mucormycosis
shortlist.why_kept: histopathological examination showed angioinvasive microbial structures and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells, consistent with Mucormycosis

shortlist.label: Aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: patient has immunocompromised state and developed febrile peak, which are risk factors for Aspergillosis

shortlist.label: Fusariosis
shortlist.why_kept: patient has neutropenia and developed skin lesions, which are common presentations of Fusariosis

shortlist.label: Entomophthoramosis
shortlist.why_kept: histopathological examination showed sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells, which are characteristic of Entomophthoramosis

shortlist.label: Scedosporiosis
shortlist.why_kept: patient has immunocompromised state and developed skin lesions, which are risk factors for Scedosporiosis

raw.rationale: The presence of angioinvasive microbial structures, sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells, and the specific characteristics of the hyphae (thin-walled, pauciseptate with minimal branching) and sporangia (thick-walled ovoid) in the histopathological examination are consistent with Mucormycosis, particularly in an immunocompromised patient with a history of neutropenia and febrile peak.

rejected.label: Aspergillosis
rejected.why: Aspergillosis typically shows more branching and septate hyphae, which does not match the histopathological findings in this case.

rejected.label: Fusariosis
rejected.why: Fusariosis is less likely given the specific morphological features of the hyphae and sporangia described, which are more characteristic of Mucormycosis.

rejected.label: Entomophthoramosis
rejected.why: Entomophthoramosis is rare and typically affects insects, making it an unlikely diagnosis in this human patient.

rejected.label: Scedosporiosis
rejected.why: Scedosporiosis might present with similar clinical manifestations but the histopathological features described are more indicative of Mucormycosis.
